family: one-person civil service orders (individual waivers, personnel designations, patent-signing designations, retirement exemptions)

mechanisms.description: A one-person permission (appointment, reinstatement, transfer, promotion, classification or exemption of a named person) can operate only for that person. It is exhausted when used and in any event cannot operate after the person's death. The death is bounded by the longest verified human life, counted from the latest date on which the order's own text shows the person alive, or from the order date less a minimum age that the text or a cited rule fixes.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Ended within (order date, bound], bound = X + 122 years 164 days, where X is the latest date at which the quoted fact shows the person alive, or the order date minus the minimum age (whole years). Use of the permission is unknown; a used permission ended earlier.

mechanisms.description: EO 209 promulgated the 1903 rules 'in lieu of those promulgated May 6, 1896, and the amendments thereof' (effective April 15, 1903). It does not plainly reach special rules (EO 250 of 1904 had to revoke a 1902 special rule), and the orders it might reach here are rule instruments, not one-person orders. Recorded only; no branch ends a member by it.

A later instrument whose words reach the member by its number, or by its date and an exact description of its subject (ruling P3): EO 5371 for EO 5332; EO 6179-A for the appointments EO 4528 and EO 5058 authorized; EO 1074 for EO 1010; EO 3075 for EO 2917; the order of July 27, 1921 for EO 1692; EO 5197-A, 5638, 5855 and 7251 superseding the radio frequency orders by number; PLO 369 for EO 2247, as BLM's official table states it.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The revoking or superseding instrument's date (fixed), or the interval (order date, revoking date] where the member is a permission whose use is unknown.

mechanisms.description: A designation or permission for a stated period ('for a period of two years', 'for a term of four years', 'ten days from the date hereof', 'for a period of one year from July 1, 1926', 'for a period of five years from March 31, 1922', 'shall terminate on July 31, 1935') ends by its own terms; an order whose only content revokes another order is spent on issue (ruling P1); an order whose only content amends another order or rule merges into the parent on issue (ruling P2): its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Order date plus the stated period, or the stated date.

mechanisms.description: General rewrites of the Civil Service Rules (EO 7916 of 1938, EO 8743 of 1941, EO 9830 of 1947, EO 10577 of 1954) revoke only listed orders and list no one-person waiver; the Act of March 27, 1922 and EO 9830 sec. 1.1(b) recognize status granted by executive order. None of these ends a member; they are recorded so that no branch relies on them.

EO 3461 (May 16, 1921) revokes 'all Executive orders ... authorizing appointments ... because of war emergencies existing at the time' and lists orders by number; the held copy stops at item 27, so the length of the list is not verified. A member whose own text rests on the war emergency is covered only on a reading of the general clause, which the machine cannot apply. No branch uses it.

Abolition by name of a body the member created (ruling P7). EO 7065 abolished the National Resources Board and its advisory committee created by EO 6777, but not the technical committee EO 6777 also established; P7 requires the abolished subject to be the member's only operative content, so no branch ends a member by it.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Would be the close of business on June 15, 1935.

procedure.description: Exemptions under sec. 204 of the 1932 Act for named persons who 'have reached' (or 'during the current month' reach) 'the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation'.

when.text_regex: (?:have reached|will reach|reach) the retire-?\s?ment age prescribed for auto-?\s?matic separation

lead.basis: The exemption can apply only to the persons named, each of whom had reached (or reached that month) a statutory retirement age, the lowest of which is 62 (S6, S7). With a minimum age of 61, every named person died no later than order date - 61 years + 122 years 164 days (at the latest 1994-06-18 for the members on this branch). The result holds for any minimum age of 29 or more (the latest member is dated January 5, 1933).

date_rule.basis: latest member 1933-01-05 minus 61 years plus 122 years 164 days

gaps: The bound rests on the longest verified human life (S1, held only on the web until acquired).
Each order names several persons; the order is spent only when every person's exemption has ended, and the bound covers all of them because each reached retirement age.
Later serial exemptions of the same persons (EO 5873, 5875 for EO 5896) do not affect the bound.

lead.basis: The death of a named person cannot end an authority that reaches a class, a list, a position or future persons; such orders end, if at all, by a later instrument that reaches them. Family: PD-CS-RULES (PD-WAR-EMERGENCY for 1917-1921 war-emergency authorities).

gaps: Re-typing to PD-CS-RULES or PD-WAR-EMERGENCY; for 1917-1921 war orders, EO 3461's full list (items 28-45).

procedure.description: Orders for a stated number of specified or named persons (lists): one act for each person named, but no fact bounds every person's death.

lead.basis: The order acts for several specified persons (often named in the text); under M1 it is spent only when every person's permission has ended, and no held fact bounds every person's death before October 14, 2026.

gaps: A dated fact for every person named (service record, Official Register), or the list's own terms.

procedure.description: Designations of a named officer to act as head of a department during absences (Rev. Stat. sec. 179) and other named-person appointments without a stated term.

lead.basis: The designation lasts while the absence lasts or until superseded, and in any event ends with the designee's tenure or death; no held field fixes the designee's minimum age or the date the designee left office.

gaps: The designee's separation or death date (Official Register, agency history, Biographical Directory); a statute fixing a minimum age for the office.

procedure.description: Retirement-act class exclusions and other retirement orders not exempting named persons.

lead.basis: These orders exclude or include classes of employees under the Retirement Act; they are not one-person exemptions. Family: PD-CS-RULES.

gaps: Re-typing; the later Retirement Act amendments and the Civil Service Retirement Act of 1956 for their effect on class exclusions.

procedure.description: Members whose WPA summary or title describes the appointee as a messenger, boy, girl or apprentice, or whose operative sentence appoints, promotes or transfers the person to or from a messenger or apprentice position (possible minors); mentions of the person's children do not count.

lead.basis: The person may have been a child at the order date; no held fact fixes a minimum age, so the death bound cannot be placed before the cutoff.

gaps: The person's birth date or separation/death (NARA St. Louis service card; Official Register; a later order naming the person).

procedure.description: One-person waivers with no held fact fixing the person's minimum age as a number, or a dated presence before May 3, 1904 (catch-all). Some state that the person was 'above the age limit' without the figure (EO 3512, 3148, 3942, 4437, 7109) or waive 'the age limit' of a postmaster examination without saying which (EO 3855).

lead.basis: The permission ended when used or at the person's death, but neither date is shown and no quoted fact bounds the death before October 14, 2026. A position or title, 'Mrs.', 'widow of', a later name match or an age limit whose figure the text does not give does not fix an adult age under the evidence rule.

gaps: Any one of: (1) the civil-service rule, Commission regulation or statute fixing the minimum or maximum age for entrance to the position's examination in force on the order date, where the order leaves the examination in place or waives a stated limit and the person is not a preference claimant (Rule V, sec. 5, numbered sec. 6 in the FY1922 printing, lets the Commission change age limits by regulation and exempts preference claimants); (2) an Official Register entry or later record dating the person's presence before May 3, 1904; (3) the NARA St. Louis service record card (birth, action and separation dates).
EO 5821 (1932) waives the 'maximum age limit' for postmaster at Woodward, Okla.; the limit then in force (EO 4919, June 22, 1928, not held) would decide it.
